title: Azure SQL Database Overview
description: Learn what Azure SQL Database is, how it compares to SQL Server, and when to use it in cloud applications.

data.text: Azure SQL Database is a fully managed relational database engine built on the latest SQL Server stable release. Microsoft handles patching, backups, high availability, and monitoring, so you can focus on database design and application development. It supports T-SQL, .NET drivers, and most tools you already know from SQL Server.

rows: One fully managed database with its own compute and storage
Multiple databases sharing a pool of compute resources
SaaS with many tenants of varying usage
Near 100% compatibility with on-premises SQL Server

data.text: You choose a compute tier (serverless or provisioned) and a storage size. Serverless auto-scales compute and pauses during inactivity. Provisioned gives you a fixed amount of compute for predictable performance. Storage is separate and can grow up to 4 TB in a single database.

data.title: Create a Single Database with Azure CLI
data.content: Provision a basic single database in a logical server
data.code:
az sql server create \
  --name sqlserver-demo \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --location eastus \
  --admin-user sqladmin \
  --admin-password '<SecurePassword>'

az sql db create \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --server sqlserver-demo \
  --name AppDb \
  --service-objective S0

terms.definition: A central administrative point for a group of databases that manages logins, firewall rules, and policies.
A fully managed database with its own dedicated compute and storage resources.
A shared compute resource for multiple databases, reducing cost for variable workloads.
Two pricing models: DTU bundles compute and storage; vCore separates them for finer control.

data.title: Managed Instance for Lift-and-Shift
data.text: If you are migrating an existing SQL Server with features like SQL Agent jobs, cross-database queries, or linked servers, use Managed Instance for near-complete compatibility.

data.title: Exercise: Create and Explore a Database
data.description: Provision an Azure SQL Database and connect with sqlcmd.
steps: Create a resource group and logical SQL server.
Allow your IP through the server firewall in the Azure Portal.
Connect using sqlcmd or Azure Data Studio and run SELECT @@VERSION.
data.expectedOutcome: A running Azure SQL Database you can query from your local machine.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure SQL Database is a fully managed, SQL Server-compatible PaaS service.
Choose single database, elastic pool, or managed instance based on your app.
Serverless compute is cost-effective for intermittent workloads.
Connection strings use the same format as SQL Server with the Azure server name.
data.takeaway: Azure SQL Database removes infrastructure work while preserving the SQL skills you already have.
